openalexAPI

Alpha. openalexAPI works and is tested, but its functions, arguments and the details of its responses may still change between versions. It is not on the openalexPro r-universe yet; install it from GitHub.

openalexAPI serves a local Parquet corpus of OpenAlex works through a web API that answers like the OpenAlex API. You can run the same queries against your own data that you run against OpenAlex: classic filter= / search= URLs, OQL (OpenAlex Query Language), OQO (OpenAlex Query Object), group_by, sort and paging. It also includes a small web page for running queries in the browser.

Because the answers look like OpenAlex’s, the download functions of openalexPro work against the local server unchanged. Point pro_query() at it with endpoint =.

The corpus can come from:

  • openalexPro::pro_request_parquet() / pro_fetch() downloads
  • an extraction from the OpenAlex snapshot (openalexSnapshot)
  • any other source with the OpenAlex works schema

It is meant for project-sized corpora, not the whole snapshot.

Installation

openalexAPI is not on the openalexPro r-universe yet. Install it from GitHub; its dependencies, openalexPro included, come along:

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("openalexPro/openalexAPI")       # main: the current alpha version
pak::pak("openalexPro/openalexAPI@dev")   # dev: the newest changes

Or with remotes:

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("openalexPro/openalexAPI")

Quick start 

library(openalexAPI)

# A corpus downloaded with openalexPro, or any folder of works Parquet files
serve_corpus("my_project/parquet", port = 8000)

Then open http://127.0.0.1:8000/ for the web page, or query the API:

http://127.0.0.1:8000/works?filter=type:article,publication_year:>2015&search=coral bleaching
http://127.0.0.1:8000/works?filter=type:article&group_by=authorships.countries
http://127.0.0.1:8000/?oql=works where type is article and year >= 2015
http://127.0.0.1:8000/works/W2741809807

From another R session, download a subset of the corpus with openalexPro, exactly as from OpenAlex:

library(openalexPro)
q <- pro_query(
  entity = "works", type = "article", search = "coral bleaching",
  endpoint = "http://127.0.0.1:8000"
)
pro_fetch(q, project_folder = "subset")

How it works 

classic URL or OQL --> OpenAlex /query (free) --> OQO --> DuckDB SQL --> OpenAlex-shaped JSON
OQO                -----------------------------^  (offline)

prepare_corpus() (run by serve_corpus()) reads the Parquet files into a cached DuckDB database. The cache holds one row per work, IDs and DOIs normalised so they match in any form, and full-text indexes over title and abstract. OpenAlex’s free /query endpoint translates classic URLs and OQL into an OQO, so the query languages are exactly OpenAlex’s. oqo_to_sql() compiles the OQO into SQL. An OQO sent directly runs without network access.

What is supported

  • 48 works filters: type, year and dates (also the creation date), language, open access, citations and percentiles, authors and ORCIDs, institutions (also with their lineage), countries, funders, sources, ISSNs, publishers, topics down to subfields, keywords, SDGs, IDs (OpenAlex, DOI, PMID, PMCID), cites and cited_by. AND, OR (a|b), negation (!a), ranges, and null for “field missing” all work.
  • group_by on one dimension, with OpenAlex’s key formats. :include_unknown is supported.
  • Full-text search over title and abstract, with search, search.exact and the <field>.search filters, plus searches in affiliation strings and author names. All words must match, quoted phrases must appear in order, proximity ("a"~N~"b", "a b"~N) works, and wildcards work with .exact. Results are ranked by relevance_score (BM25).
  • Records are returned as stored, including fields that are not OpenAlex’s. You can use select, sort, per_page, page, cursor and sample/seed, and look up single works by ID or DOI.

Differences from OpenAlex

  • Local data: counts come from the corpus, not from all of OpenAlex.
  • Search covers title and abstract only, because there is no full text. The stemmer folds more word forms than OpenAlex’s, so stemmed counts can be higher. Proximity allows up to N words between the terms, an approximation of OpenAlex’s.
  • Display names: countries, languages and licenses use the code as the display name in group_by results (“AU” rather than “Australia”).
  • Unsupported features get a clear HTTP 400 that names them: OpenAlex collections, semantic search, group_by on several dimensions, and OQL’s comparisons and nested queries. 156 of OpenAlex’s 174 OQL example queries run locally (tools/oql_coverage.R).

See vignette("openalexAPI") for the details.
